problem: The sensor expected 20 input fields but the update supplied 21, causing an out-of-bounds memory read and a system crash; a Content Validator bug let the problematic content through.
title: CrowdStrike ships a faulty content update that crashes millions of Windows devices
context: A Falcon sensor content update went out at 04:09 UTC on 19 July 2024.
decision_made: Release the content update to all customers at once, then revert it at 05:27 UTC.
action_taken: Published a root cause analysis in August 2024 and committed to staged deployment starting with a canary group, customer control over rollout, more testing including fuzzing, and added bounds checks.
observed_outcome: More than eight million devices worldwide reportedly crashed. Systems that came online after the revert or did not connect in the window were not impacted.
observation_period: Hours of impact, with remediation over following weeks
lessons: Even content updates need staged rollout, validation and bounds checking when they run at kernel level.
limitations: The 8.5 million figure was not found in the sources, which say more than eight million. Financial and legal consequences were not covered here.

claims.claim_text: CrowdStrike's update expected 20 input fields but supplied 21, causing an out-of-bounds read and system crash.
CrowdStrike committed to staged deployment starting with canary deployments for Rapid Response Content.
